extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty, assessment coordinators, and college/university educators involved in undergraduate program assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for assessing undergraduate mathematics majors, including portfolio requirements, departmental testing (MFT), senior presentations, course-embedded diagnostic projects, and entry-level reform recommendations. Aimed at designing, implementing, and using assessment measures to improve curricula and student learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student portfolio contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Portfolios should include examinations and samples of students' best work from each mathematics class; a copy of any research or expository paper in an upper level class should also be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios are intended to provide evidence of how well students synthesize and integrate knowledge from different courses and to indicate that a student can use various approaches to solve problems. Samples are to be collected for the portfolio by advisors during formal advising periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry profile contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry profile contains information on a student prior to enrolling at the University, such as the mathematics courses taken in high school, grade point average and rank in graduating class, SAT and/or ACT scores, and advanced placement (AP) credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The profile also contains placement scores from University-administered exams in mathematics and foreign language; it is used to document incoming preparation and to inform placement/advising decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance questionnaire (fall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short questionnaire given in the fall term revealing the student's perception of mathematics and his/her expectations of the program and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside the entry profile to capture student attitudes and expectations early in the program; informs advising and program adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Major Field Test (MFT) in Mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department administers the Major Field Test (MFT) in Mathematics (ETS), which reports individual and mean scores plus subscores that point out strengths and weaknesses in broad areas within mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MFT replaced the GRE Advanced test as a better match to the student profile; subscores are valuable for diagnosing curricular strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: MFT departmental performance threshold and follow-up policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has set as successful performance a score at the 60% mark or higher; this mark is not rigidly enforced and the Department undertakes an extensive study of the individual case whenever this goal is not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the goal is not met, a recommendation is made whether to pass the student or ask the student to retake the exam. Students may request a departmental comprehensive exam after two unsuccessful MFT performances; unsatisfactory performance there may lead to advising toward a liberal arts degree. Review sessions for seniors are provided in the fall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior presentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each senior is required to make an oral presentation (a thirty-minute lecture) with the topic selected by the student and approved by the advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisor provides a list of helpful steps, feedback on a written draft, and arranges practice sessions; the presentation is intended to help students synthesize mathematical concepts and perfect skills covered in courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exit and alumni questionnaires/surveys schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Exit questionnaires are sent to graduating seniors about three weeks prior to the end of the spring semester and exit interviews are scheduled; an alumni survey will be administered every five years; alumni questionnaires are mailed one year after graduation in intervening years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments track placement of graduates, gather feedback on courses and faculty, and inform curricular and advising changes; different forms have different breadth and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio evidence expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Portfolios should provide an evolving picture of mathematical growth and progress, evidence of content, level of difficulty, and teaching philosophy in mathematics courses for majors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios supply information about the manner in which a course is taught that is not available from course evaluations; as more students/courses are tracked, portfolios give a more thorough understanding of the overall curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of student feedback in curricular decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information from exit questionnaires, alumni surveys, and interviews (e.g., requests for more electives, concerns about discrete mathematics, reactions to technology use) should be used to review and revise curriculum and course content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments should respond to recurring themes (e.g., balance of technology like MAPLE, course accessibility, career counseling) by reviewing course content, cycle of electives, and advising practices; communicate feedback to individual faculty when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding assessment in courses (Sophomore–Junior Diagnostic Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sophomore–Junior Diagnostic Project is embedded in a required course (Discrete Mathematics) and revolves around a substantial expository paper spanning the entire semester; it is a graded component (counts one-fourth of the course grade).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project is intended as a checkpoint to identify students needing remediation and as a 'pump' to impel all students toward greater facility in gathering and communicating information; it should be course-embedded rather than an isolated gate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project structure and interim deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project begins with a memo from the instructor indicating the assigned topic; after beginning research the student submits a progress memo accompanied by a proposed outline and an annotated bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated bibliographies indicate the role each reference will play and assure adequate resource gathering and appropriate scope (target ≈10 double-spaced pages). Early memos can reveal writing difficulties and trigger referrals to writing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision, conferencing, and weighting policy for Project drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Students submit an 'initial formal draft' and receive detailed, personalized guidance in a conference with the instructor; the final draft is counted twice as much toward the project grade as the first draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring revision and a conference is crucial; the initial draft is expected to meet same specifications as final and the conference is the most powerful learning experience for improving communication skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral presentation component and practice run
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project includes a formal oral presentation (with overhead projector); students make a first attempt (practice run) and receive feedback before the final graded presentation. The practice run has no impact on the grade and the student may choose whether the instructor attends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice runs often occur in front of classmates who provide suggestions; peer feedback improves final presentations and student comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation 'crutches' (written and oral evaluation forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation forms for the written report and oral presentation contain sections on content, organization, and mechanics; each section lists questions to focus the evaluator and provide space for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are not true-false checklists but guides to help instructors (often untrained in judging writing/speaking) focus on aspects such as effective use of overheads and clear articulation; use forms tailored to mathematical exposition rather than generic speech class forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer evaluation use and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer evaluations of oral presentations are valuable: they make students more conscious of expectations, provide second opinions, and improve final presentations. However, peer responses can vary widely in homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors must decide how to handle lack of consensus in peer feedback and how to judge subjective qualities (e.g., presentation 'beauty'); peer feedback is primarily formative but can inform instructor judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Incomplete' grade for remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow a course grade of 'Incomplete' for a passing student whose Project reveals inadequate mastery of writing skills; the instructor converts the grade to a letter grade when satisfied the student has remedied deficiencies (e.g., worked with the Writing Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy provides leverage to ensure remediation beyond the course term and supports follow-up learning for deficiencies uncovered by the Project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary success factors for course-embedded Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Key factors are (1) giving feedback rather than a mere grade, (2) providing guidance/specifications/examples/demonstrations and the evaluation forms, and (3) follow-up remediation when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit expectations and ongoing support (specifications, suggestions, examples, demonstrations) plus feedback and remediation lead to stronger learning outcomes than grading alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit-hour and workload recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses administering intensive, semester-spanning Projects should recognize additional workload (e.g., course earns four credit-hours while meeting only three hours per week; extra meetings scheduled for presentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging instructor workload (modest overload pay) and giving course credit commensurate with out-of-class mentoring/time encourages faculty involvement in intensive assessment activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental goals (University of Arizona)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overarching goals include: (1) provide flexible yet solid undergraduate and graduate programs; (2) prepare an ethnically diverse spectrum of entering students; (3) embrace change (e.g., technology, reform) to enhance learning; (4) be a resource in mathematical sciences for other disciplines; (5) work closely with local schools and community colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals frame departmental assessment priorities across research, teaching, outreach, and collaboration; they guide program-level changes and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-level assessment premises (Arizona Entry Level Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five fundamental premises: (1) students must be placed in courses commensurate with abilities and background; (2) provide a supportive learning environment and caring instructors; (3) entry-level courses must be structured to meet current student needs; (4) effective outreach to local schools is essential; (5) students need exposure to technology to enhance learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These premises underlie entry-level reform plans and inform specific recommendations (placement tests, advising, course redesign, technology integration, outreach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-level action plan recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Key recommendations: reduce class size; institute a mandatory math placement and advising program; institute a new precalculus course; introduce a Calculus I course with five credit hours; replace self-study algebra with a two-semester college algebra sequence (noting later upgrade to a one-semester four-credit algebra course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are operational steps to realize the premises (better placement, structured courses, smaller sections, and credit-hour alignment); implementation accompanied by resource estimates and multi-year planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular program review mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internal and external review committees, exit surveys of majors, and periodic departmental reviews to assess freshman and undergraduate programs and to document findings and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should examine enrollment, pass/fail rates, interviews with stakeholders, and result in actionable plans (e.g., five-year implementation plans) and resource requests; findings drive committee formation and reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Center and student support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Create centralized resources (Mathematics Center) providing library materials, a full-time advisor, lockers, computer facilities, upper-division tutoring, an undergraduate colloquium, and information about graduate schools, careers, and summer programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support centers and dedicated advising/tutoring infrastructure are identified as contributors to increased major numbers and improved undergraduate outcomes; assessment evidence should support funding and expansion.
